steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — Identify the deadline date.** Saturday, Oct 24, 2026 + 6 days = Friday, Oct 30, 2026. (Consistent with "on Friday.")

**Step 2 — Which PT offset?** US daylight saving ends Sunday, Nov 1, 2026, so Oct 30 is still PDT = UTC−7. So 11:59 PM PDT = 06:59 UTC on Oct 31, 2026.

**Step 3 — Madrid offset.** EU summer time ended Sunday, Oct 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET = UTC+1. 06:59 UTC + 1h = 07:59 local, Saturday, Oct 31, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**

- "This coming Monday" from Friday, Oct 30, 2026 → **Monday, November 2, 2026**.
- US DST ends Sunday, Nov 1, 2026, so Los Angeles is on **PST (UTC−8)** → 10:00 PST = 18:00 UTC.
- EU DST ended Sunday, Oct 25, 2026, so Madrid is on **CET (UTC+1)** → 18:00 UTC = 19:00 local.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**

- Start: Sat 24 Oct 2026, 18:00 Madrid time. Spain is on CEST (UTC+2) then → 16:00 UTC.
- Exactly 48 hours later = Mon 26 Oct 2026, 16:00 UTC.
- But DST ends on Sunday 25 October 2026 (clocks go back 03:00 → 02:00), so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1) by Monday.
- 16:00 UTC + 1h = 17:00 Madrid time.

So the hackathon ends at 17:00 local on Monday, October 26 — i.e., the wall clock shows one hour "less" than 18:00 because of the extra hour gained.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — Start in UTC:** US Pacific DST ends Nov 1, 2026, so Oct 26 is PDT (UTC−7). 10:00 PDT = 17:00 UTC.

**Step 2 — Add 72 hours:** 17:00 UTC on Oct 29, 2026.

**Step 3 — Convert to Madrid:** EU summer time ended Sunday, Oct 25, 2026, so Spain is on CET (UTC+1). 17:00 UTC → 18:00 local.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — Closing time in UTC.**
US daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday of November = Nov 1, 2026. So on Oct 31, 2026, Eastern Time is still EDT (UTC−4).
Oct 31, 2026, 11:59 PM EDT = Nov 1, 2026, 03:59 UTC.

**Step 2 — Add 36 hours.**
Nov 1, 03:59 UTC + 36 h = Nov 2, 2026, 15:59 UTC.
(Using a fixed UTC offset avoids any ambiguity from the US clock change on Nov 1.)

**Step 3 — Convert to Madrid time.**
EU summer time ended on the last Sunday of October = Oct 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).
15:59 UTC + 1 h = 16:59 on Nov 2, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — Convert to UTC:** 1791788340 s → 2026‑10‑12 06:59:00 UTC.

**Step 2 — Apply Tokyo offset:** Japan is UTC+9 year‑round (no DST), so add 9 hours → 2026‑10‑12 15:59 JST (a Monday).

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**

- Madrid is UTC+2 (CEST) in summer, UTC+1 (CET) in winter.
- EU summer time ends on the last Sunday of October, which in 2026 is **October 25**, with the change happening at **01:00 UTC** (clocks go 03:00 CEST → 02:00 CET).
- The deadline, 02:30 UTC, falls **after** that 01:00 UTC switch, so Madrid is already on CET (UTC+1).
- 02:30 UTC + 1 hour = **03:30 local time** on 2026-10-25.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 – Find the date:** October 2026 Sundays are 4, 11, 18, 25 (Nov 1 is the next one), so the last Sunday is **October 25, 2026**.

**Step 2 – Pacific Time offset:** U.S. daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday of November (Nov 1, 2026), so Oct 25 is still PDT = UTC−7. Deadline = Oct 25, 23:59 PDT = **Oct 26, 06:59 UTC**.

**Step 3 – Madrid offset:** EU summer time ends on the last Sunday of October — Oct 25, 2026 at 01:00 UTC — so by Oct 26 Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

**Step 4 – Convert:** 06:59 UTC + 1 h = 07:59 on Monday, October 26, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 – Find the date.** In the US, daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday in November. In 2026, November 1 is a Sunday, so the deadline date is **Sunday, November 1, 2026**.

**Step 2 – Determine the Eastern offset at noon that day.** The changeover happens at 2:00 a.m. local daylight time, when clocks fall back to 1:00 a.m. EST. By 12:00 noon, the Eastern Time Zone is already on **EST = UTC−5**.

**Step 3 – Convert to Lima.** Peru uses PET = UTC−5 all year (no DST). So noon EST = 12:00 UTC−5 = 12:00 in Lima — the same clock reading.

(Note: had the deadline been *before* 2 a.m., Eastern would still have been EDT = UTC−4 and you'd subtract an hour. At noon, there's no difference.)

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**
- AoE (Anywhere on Earth) = UTC−12.
- "December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE" = the instant 2027‑01‑01 00:00 at UTC−12.
- Convert to UTC: add 12 h → 2027‑01‑01 12:00 UTC.
- Tokyo is JST = UTC+9, no daylight saving → add 9 h → 2027‑01‑01 21:00.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1 — Sydney offset on Oct 5, 2026:** Australian DST begins the first Sunday in October, which is Oct 4, 2026. So Sydney is on AEDT = UTC+11.

5:00 PM AEDT, Oct 5 → 06:00 UTC, Oct 5.

**Step 2 — New York offset:** US DST runs until the first Sunday in November, so New York is on EDT = UTC−4.

06:00 UTC − 4h = 02:00 on Oct 5, 2026.

(For reference, in Madrid that would be 08:00 CEST — but since you're in New York that week, the deadline hits at 2:00 AM local.)

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
